answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, with the stake slashed when a randomly audited task reveals fabricated work. Audits sample across a reef of task types, so an attacker cannot cheaply train one convincing sable persona and reuse it everywhere. Creating a dune of identities multiplies the capital tied up and the chance of a costly slash; identities gain influence only as they complete verified work, making mass registration expensive without relying on names or device fingerprints.
